tasks.goal: A new package services/api/app/narrative with three pure parts. (1) collector: given a period ('bu hafta' = the last 7 days, 'bugün', 'dün', or explicit start/end in UTC) and an optional device word (ev / ofis / bulut / a device name), read the activity ledger through the existing read-only query in app/ledger/service.py (query / latest - read that file first; do not change it) and produce a NarrativeFacts dataclass: failed events FIRST (each with its subsystem, summary and the reason the ledger holds), then completed events grouped by subsystem, counts per subsystem and per device, no_capable_device events, and the period actually covered. Deterministic: the same rows give the same facts. (2) narrator: a Protocol `Narrator.tell(facts) -> str` with a RuleNarrator that writes Turkish sentences from the facts alone (no model call in this task; the model narrator is a later task behind the same Protocol) - about 30 seconds of speech, failures first, then what was done, then counts; an empty period says 'bu dönemde kayıt yok'. (3) auditor: `audit(facts, text) -> Verdict` that REJECTS a narrative in which any failed event is not mentioned (match by its summary words), any completed subsystem is missing, or a number appears that is not one of the facts' counts; and `repair(facts, text)` that appends the missing failure sentences deterministically. The public entry is `tell(db, period, device=None, narrator=None) -> str` = collect → narrate → audit → repair. Read docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-0201 and the ledger vocabulary for the event types and statuses; use their constants by import, never string copies. Work only inside the area. Do not edit docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, state/BUILD_STATE.json, docs/THIRD_PARTY_COMPONENTS.md, app/ledger/vocabulary.py or any file outside the area: the lead wires shared files at merge time from your report. No new dependency. Python 3.12, ruff clean, tests under services/api/tests/unit run with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest <file> -q` from services/api. Every test name is a sentence about behaviour; every rule has a near miss beside its hit; one mutation per rule shown RED and the file restored by sha256 (never git checkout --).
tasks.acceptance: test_narrative_collector.py: a fixed set of ledger rows (SQLite, the ledger's own model) with failed and completed events across two devices and three subsystems; the facts put failures first; 'ofiste' selects the office device's rows only; 'bu hafta' and 'dün' cover exactly the rows in their window; an empty period yields empty facts; the same rows twice give equal facts. test_narrative_auditor.py: a narrative that omits one failure is rejected and repair adds it; a narrative with a number not in the facts is rejected; the RuleNarrator's output passes the auditor for every fixture; tell() over the SQLite rows returns Turkish text that names every failure. Mutations: the collector drops one failure → auditor RED; the auditor's number check disabled → RED. ruff clean.

tasks.title: Bulutta yürütme: execution_target kuralı (cloud / owner_chrome / device), düşüş zinciri ve olayları — saf kural tablosu (öneri 1, PR 1)
tasks.goal: A new package services/api/app/execution holding the execution_target decision as pure functions - nothing here talks to a device, a database or a model. Inputs: a JobKind (research, browser_task, desktop, scheduled, compute), what the owner said (a spoken target word: 'bulutta' / 'bulut' forces cloud; a named device or alias forces that device; ADR-0212's spoken-device rule stays the device layer's - you only take the resolved word), the site's needs (needs_signed_in_session, on the task deny-list of packages/protocol/browser-task-denylist.json - read it, do not copy it), and the availability of each target (cloud online, owner Chrome enrolled and its device online, named device online). Output: a Decision with the chosen target, the ORDERED fallback chain that was considered, and one reason code per skipped target. Rules, each with a test: scheduled jobs always run in the cloud and never fall back to the owner's Chrome; research defaults to cloud, then owner_chrome, then device; a job that needs a signed-in session defaults to owner_chrome and NEVER to cloud; desktop jobs run on the device and never in the cloud; compute runs in the cloud only; a forced target that is unavailable is a refusal with reason `forced_target_unavailable`, not a silent fallback; a cloud run that meets an auth wall, a CAPTCHA or a challenge does not fall back on its own - the decision says `ask_owner` (ADR-0207 decision 6); payment is out of scope everywhere; the deny-list refuses acting (not reading) on every target. Also: `events(decision)` returns the ledger event records to write (`execution.selected`, `execution.fallback` with the reason, `execution.refused`) as plain dicts with an event_type key - define the three event-type strings as constants in app/execution/vocabulary.py; the lead registers them in app/ledger/vocabulary.py at merge. Write team/plans/execution-target-rule-adr.md: the rule table as a markdown table, the fallback chain, and the open question of where the owner's 'no unattended task' (ADR-0207 decision 3) stands for a cloud job (state the options; decide nothing). Work only inside the area. Do not edit docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, state/BUILD_STATE.json, docs/THIRD_PARTY_COMPONENTS.md, app/ledger/vocabulary.py or any file outside the area: the lead wires shared files at merge time from your report. No new dependency. Python 3.12, ruff clean, tests under services/api/tests/unit run with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest <file> -q` from services/api. Every test name is a sentence about behaviour; every rule has a near miss beside its hit; one mutation per rule shown RED and the file restored by sha256 (never git checkout --).
tasks.acceptance: test_execution_target.py: every rule above has its test with a near miss (e.g. 'bulut' inside a site name is not a forced target; a device alias that resolves to no device is `forced_target_unavailable`); the fallback chain is ordered and complete for each JobKind; scheduled never reaches owner_chrome even when cloud is offline (refused); needs_signed_in_session never reaches cloud; events() produces exactly one execution.selected or execution.refused per decision and one execution.fallback per skipped target, each with a reason. Mutations: the scheduled→owner_chrome guard removed → RED; the signed-in guard removed → RED; the forced-target refusal turned into a fallback → RED. ruff clean.
